{{nihongo|''jagaimo''|[[wiktionary:ジャガ芋|ジャガ芋]]||lit. 'Jakarta tuber/root vegetable', 'potato'}}<ref name="d" />}}}} is a [[Japanese cuisine|Japanese dish]] of [[meat]], [[potato]]es, and [[onion|onions]] stewed in [[dashi]], [[soy sauce]], [[mirin]], and [[sugar]], sometimes with ''[[ito konnyaku]]'' and vegetables like [[Carrot|carrots]].<ref name="d">{{cite encyclopedia|encyclopedia=Dijitaru Daijisen |title=肉ジャガ |url=http://rekishi.jkn21.com/ |access-date=2012-08-27 |year=2012 |publisher=Shogakukan |location=Tokyo |language=ja |trans-title=Nikujaga |oclc=56431036 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070825113418/http://rekishi.jkn21.com/ |archive-date=August 25, 2007 }}</ref> Nikujaga is a kind of ''[[nimono]]''. It is usually boiled until most of the liquid has been [[Reduction (cooking)|reduced]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = 肉じゃがのレシピ｜キユーピー3分クッキング|url = http://www.ntv.co.jp/3min/recipe/20150415.html|website = 日本テレビ|access-date = 2015-10-31|language = ja}}</ref> Thinly sliced beef is the most common meat used, although minced or ground beef is also popular.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = ★激論★ 肉じゃがといえば、豚か、牛か! それとも何か!? {{!}} クックパッド|url = http://cookpad.com/articles/100|website = クックパッド|access-date = 2015-10-31}}</ref> Pork is often used instead of beef in eastern Japan.<ref name=":0" />
During [[World War II]], it was served as a navy dish. Today, people make it as one of the home dishes and eat it regardless of seasons.
Nikujaga is a common home-cooked winter dish, served with a bowl of white rice and [[miso soup]]. It is also sometimes seen in ''[[izakaya]]s''.{{citation needed|date=November 2012}}
